summary: Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Urach, Heidelberg, Jena, and Tübingen—earning a Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth—he taught at the Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminaries before becoming professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studies at Munich, Berlin, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Haug, Weber, and Brockhaus, he served as Tagore professor of law at Calcutta (1882–1883) and professor at Würzburg (1877–1920).

Julius Jüthner (1866–1945) was an Austrian scholar in archaeology and history. He studied at the German University of Prague and held academic posts at the University of Fribourg (around 1898–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (around 1912–1937).

Julius Klaproth (1783–1835) was a specialist in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student at the University of Halle in 1801, he founded the Asiatisches Magazin and held a chair at the University of Bonn (~1816–1835).

Julius Laber (1884–1944) was an Indologist. He pursued his education at the universities of Berlin, Freiburg, Leipzig, and Bonn, completing his Ph.D. at Bonn in 1913 and studying under Hermann Jacobi in 1908.

Julius Leumann was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Geneva, Zurich, Leipzig, and Strasbourg, where he completed his Ph.D. in 1893. He later served as a teacher (1898) and rector (1906–1928) at Kantonsschule Frauenfeld.

Julius Lipner (born 1946) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Jadavpur, Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis, he lectured at Birmingham before serving as professor of Hinduism at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl (1800–1876) worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, he held professorships at Tübingen (1826–1834) and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller (1801–1878) worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Breslau, Berlin, and Göttingen, he held academic appointments at the universities of Göttingen (~1831–1835), Marburg (~1835–1839), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny (1887–1970) worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Vienna under Kretschmer and Much, he held posts at Vienna, Berlin (1920–1935 as professor of Celtology), Bern, Zurich, Fribourg, Kiel, Munich, and Erlangen-Nuremberg.
Julius Schubring (1839–1914) studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1857–1858), the University of Bonn (~1858–1860), and the University of Göttingen (~1860–1862).

Julius Schwab (1852–1928) was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1874–1882) under Martin Haug and Ernst Kuhn. He worked at the Badische Landesbibliothek (1882) and as a librarian at Freiburg University Library (1887).

Julius Wellhausen (1844–1918) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and held posts at the universities of Greifswald (~1872–1882), Halle-Wittenberg (~1882–1885), Marburg (~1885–1892), and Göttingen (~1892–1913).

Julius von Negelein (1872–1932) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Greifswald, Berlin, Marburg, and Königsberg (Ph.D.), served as Privatdozent at Königsberg (1899), and became full professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1920.

Juliusz J. Ossowski (1855–1882) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Königsberg (Ph.D.) under Adalbert Bezzenberger and Richard von Garbe.

Jun Fujii (born 1976) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo (~2003–2007), he joined Komazawa University as a full-time lecturer (~2010–2013) and became a professor there in 2025.

Jun Takashima (born 1955) works in Indology, religious studies, and computational fields. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, he held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1993) and as professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2020.

Jun Yang specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang serves as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University and as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago.

Jundo Nagashima is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bristol (PhD under Paul Williams) and under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson, Nagashima has held posts at Taisho University and its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

June McDaniel is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned an MTS at Emory University and a Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (1980–1986), becoming Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston in 1988.
